title: Setting the scene
intro: A few framing questions before the details — these shape how the rest gets told.

fields.label: What time period does this story cover?
What feeling or message do you want to come through?
fields.placeholder: e.g. resilience, quiet courage, the cost of small kindnesses

fields.label: What's your relationship to the person this story is about?
fields.placeholder: e.g. granddaughter, told to me by my mother

title: Life before the war
intro: Who they were before everything changed.

fields.label: What name were they born with, and what were they called growing up?
fields.placeholder: Birth name, nicknames, any name changes later

fields.label: When and where were they born?
Who were the close and extended family around them?
Did religion, tradition, or culture shape their everyday life?

title: The war years
intro: What's known about this period — even fragments are worth writing down.

fields.label: Where was the family during the war?
Was there a song, phrase, or story that gave them strength?
Was there a moment they had to make a hard decision?
fields.placeholder: Describe the moment, as much as is known

fields.label: Did anyone help or support them along the way?

title: After the war
intro: Liberation is rarely the end of the story — what came next is often the part a family knows best.

fields.label: Did they return home after the war?
fields.placeholder: What they found, or why they couldn't go back

fields.label: Did they spend time in the displaced persons camps?
When did they come to Israel, or emigrate elsewhere?
What did they build afterwards?
fields.placeholder: Work, the family they made, the life that followed

title: A message for today
intro: What this story is for, beyond remembering it.

fields.label: Why does it matter to you to share this now?
What would you want future generations to take from it?
What do you hope listeners carry with them?
